answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must lock stake in a cryptographic vault like a crystal, burning a quadratic fee $B(n)=k \cdot n^2$ for every $n$-th identity registered within an epoch. This enforces superlinear attacker cost while legitimate activity triggers only a minimal ripple across network state. Expired registration proofs are archived as an immutable relic to audit past commitments, making large-scale coordination mathematically prohibitive.
